headline: Research Local Access and Dark Sky Guidelines
reservation: Entry to the park is generally free and open, but separate booking is necessary for specific services like activity centres or guided tours. Accommodation varies from canal boats to bunkhouses and hotels, all requiring independent reservations. Check with the National Park Authority for current policies on organized events or commercial group access.

days.title: Central Peaks and Canal Heritage

stops.name: Monmouthshire and Brecon Canal Towpath
stops.detail: Walk a scenic section of this historic waterway, known for its spectacular views and peaceful environment.

stops.name: Pen y Fan
stops.detail: Hike the highest peak in southern Britain for extensive views across the sandstone massifs.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local travel; conditions vary by narrow lane access
days.note: Pacing is a suggestion; mountain weather changes rapidly on the central summits.

days.title: Waterfalls and Industrial History

stops.name: Taf Fechan River Walk
stops.detail: Follow a moderate circular trail through ancient woodlands alongside the river.

stops.name: Blaenavon UNESCO World Heritage Site
stops.detail: Explore the region's magnificent industrial heritage and early mining history.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; conditions vary on rural routes
days.note: Industrial sites may have specific visiting schedules; allow extra time for exploring.

days.title: Western Castles and Caves

stops.name: Carreg Cennen Castle
stops.detail: Visit this historic fortress perched on a steep limestone crag overlooking the valley.

stops.name: National Showcaves Centre
stops.detail: Experience the park's karst geology through one of its most famous underground attractions.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours total; conditions vary with western terrain
days.note: Western routes pass through wilder country; navigation skills are recommended for off-trail areas.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking is available at major hubs like the National Park Visitor Centre and Pen y Pass. Popular spots fill early during peak walking seasons.

intel.title: Remote Connectivity
intel.text: Mobile reception is often unreliable in deep valleys and high moorland areas. Download maps for the Black Mountains and Fforest Fawr before departure.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Fuel is best found in larger market towns such as Brecon, Abergavenny, or Llandeilo. Rural villages may lack 24-hour service stations.

intel.title: Dark Sky Stargazing
intel.text: As an International Dark Sky Reserve, the park offers optimal viewing of the Milky Way on clear nights. Plan evening visits to designated dark sky spots.

intel.title: Farming Landscape
intel.text: Much of the park is a working landscape with active farming and livestock. Always follow the Countryside Code and keep dogs under control near sheep.

plan.arrival: First two hours: Pick up rental in Cardiff or Swansea, drive north to Brecon for supplies and local maps at the visitor centre.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for most roads, but check rental restrictions for narrow country lanes and steep gradients.
plan.goldenHour: Hay Bluff offers sunset views over the valley, though visibility is highly season-dependent.
